messages.content: Idaho update: the office approved it as mileage instead of the open-jaw flight. I’ll have two boxes of admitted-student materials, and the one-way rental fee made flying look bad. The Boise reception moved downtown with garage parking; Nampa counselor breakfast is 7:30 Wednesday; Twin Falls transfer table ends 4:30; Pocatello high-school visit is still 8:30 Thursday. Can you narrow the drive plan and which refundable rooms to hold?

Yes. The car plan is cleaner now. I’d set the overnights as Tuesday in Nampa and Wednesday in Pocatello. Downtown Boise is convenient after the reception but makes the 7:30 Nampa breakfast unnecessarily tight. The only reliability question is Monday night: add a weather-buffer room only if I-84 looks rough; otherwise an early Tuesday drive from Salt Lake City works.
Let’s make Monday weather-only. I can leave early Tuesday, but I do not want Wednesday morning to be a scramble.

Then Tuesday should be: leave SLC around 6:30-7:00, fuel or coffee before/around Burley, reach downtown Boise with a lunch cushion, park in the venue garage, and head to Nampa after the reception. Area tradeoff: Nampa is best for the 7:30 breakfast and free parking; west Meridian has more dinner choices but a longer morning; Boise is least helpful for Wednesday.
Nampa it is. I need breakfast early enough to grab something before 7:30, and I’d rather not pay hotel parking with the boxes in the car.

Hold a refundable Nampa room near Idaho Center or the Civic Center with free parking, interior corridors, breakfast starting by 6:00 or confirmed grab-and-go, and a request for a well-lit lot side. At check-in, ask whether the desk can store the materials overnight; if not, keep them covered and out of sight.
What’s the best Pocatello area? I just need practical: easy arrival from Twin Falls, food nearby, and not far from the 8:30 visit.

Use the I-15/Bench Road side unless the school visit is far south. It is easiest coming from Twin Falls and leaving for Salt Lake after the visit. The ISU side can be closer to some schools, but there are fewer simple dinner choices right after a long fair day.
Okay, I-15 side. No prepaid rooms. Queen if selectable, but flag it if the refundable inventory only shows something odd.

Shortlist to hold: Nampa Tuesday night at a refundable Hampton or Holiday Inn Express near Idaho Center/Civic Center; free parking, early breakfast, non-smoking queen if available. Pocatello Wednesday night at a refundable Fairfield, Hampton, or Holiday Inn Express near I-15; free parking, breakfast if available, nearby casual dinner. Keep a Twin Falls/Jerome Monday weather-room candidate ready, but do not hold it unless the forecast worsens.
Add the downtown Boise garage and materials notes so I can send a clean plan to my supervisor.

Supervisor-ready version: drive the full Idaho swing because the car carries two materials boxes and avoids one-way rental charges. Tuesday: SLC to downtown Boise, use venue garage for the reception, then stay in Nampa for the 7:30 counselor breakfast. Wednesday: Nampa to Twin Falls, table until 4:30, then Pocatello I-15-area overnight. Thursday: 8:30 Pocatello visit, then return to Salt Lake. Hold only refundable rooms with free parking and early breakfast; ask hotels about secure materials storage at check-in.

Good. I’ll need to leave the hotel by about 7:05 for the breakfast, so breakfast at 6 works. What did Pocatello look like?

Pocatello is in place: Fairfield Inn & Suites Pocatello, Wednesday Feb. 26, refundable non-smoking king, free parking, breakfast 6:30-9:30, cancellation by 6:00 PM Feb. 25. It is close to I-15 and a short drive from casual restaurants; it is not a full-service dinner hotel, so I’d plan dinner before fully settling in.
That’s fine. Please note restaurant access, but don’t make it sound like the hotel has dinner onsite. After Twin Falls, I just need easy.

Noted. Wednesday timing: leave Nampa after the counselor breakfast, drive toward Twin Falls with a fuel stop if needed, work the transfer table until 4:30, pack out by 4:45, and arrive Pocatello around 6:30-7:00 in normal conditions. Easy dinner candidates near the hotel are Jakers, Sandpiper, or takeout on the way in; check hours before leaving Twin Falls.
Can you map the materials handoff points? That’s the part my supervisor keeps asking about.

Materials flow: load both boxes in SLC Tuesday. Boise reception materials go from the car to the downtown venue via the garage, then leftovers return to the car after the event. Keep Nampa counselor packets in a separate tote so Wednesday morning is quick. Twin Falls table materials stay packed until setup, then get repacked before the Pocatello drive. Thursday school packets should ride separately in the front tote.
Last piece: mileage, parking, and meal receipts. The garage receipt is the one I’m most likely to forget.

Reservation and reimbursement packet: Nampa and Pocatello refundable rooms are held; both include free parking and breakfast, with Nampa supporting the early departure and Pocatello set as a practical arrival/return point. No Monday weather room is held yet. Save the Boise garage receipt, meal receipts within per diem, and final hotel folios. Keep fuel receipts only if your office asks for the trip file; mileage reimbursement usually covers fuel. Record starting and ending odometer or attach the mapped SLC-Boise-Nampa-Twin Falls-Pocatello-SLC route. Rationale sentence: Driving is the approved lower-friction option because the trip requires transporting two boxes of admitted-student materials across multiple stops and avoids open-jaw airfare plus one-way rental/drop fees.

messages.content: I’m two days out on Idaho. Forecast now shows a snow band on I-84 between Burley and Twin Falls Tuesday morning, and the Boise venue moved the materials drop to 3:30 PM. Nampa says they can do a grab-and-go breakfast. Also, the restaurant closest to the Pocatello hotel is closed Wednesday. I’d like to avoid rebuilding the trip unless Tuesday gets too tight.

I would not rebuild yet. Keep the Tuesday departure, but set a real cutoff. If Monday evening still shows open roads and no heavy I-84 warning, leave early Tuesday. If the band shifts earlier, road status turns red, or the forecast pushes the SLC-Boise drive past about 6.5 hours, add the Monday night buffer in Twin Falls/Jerome.
I can leave by 5:15 Tuesday. What should I check and when?

Monday 6:00 PM: check ID 511 and the NWS point forecast for Burley, Jerome, and Twin Falls. If closures, chain restrictions, or heavy snow are likely after 6:00 AM Tuesday, book the buffer. Tuesday 4:45 AM: if roads are open and moving, go; if I-84 is closed, call the Boise venue and your supervisor before leaving.
Okay, no Monday room unless that trigger hits. Where should I stop?

Fuel Monday night in Salt Lake. Tuesday, make only short stops: Snowville or Malta if needed, then Jerome/Twin Falls once you are through the worst of the band. Avoid making Burley the planned long stop if conditions are active. Target Boise by 1:30, which still protects the 3:30 drop.
Does the grab-and-go change Wednesday morning?

Yes: request it at Nampa check-in, leave by 7:05 with only the counselor tote, and keep the rest packed. After the breakfast, top off fuel in Nampa or Jerome, then continue to Twin Falls with lunch buffer before the table.
Pick the Pocatello dinner and give me the tiny checklist.

Use Jakers near I-15 as the first dinner plan; call from Twin Falls when you pack out. If the wait is long, switch to takeout and eat at the hotel. Tiny checklist: Monday 6 PM road decision; Tuesday 4:45 AM road check; fuel before leaving SLC; boxes covered and separated by event; Boise garage receipt; Nampa grab-and-go request; Wednesday dinner call before leaving Twin Falls; save hotel folios, garage, meals, and any required fuel receipts; pack scraper, gloves, boots, charger, badge/QR, table cloth, name tags, and extra pens.
